svg.aria-label: wireframe schematic — the app’s own layout, drawn frame by frame: the given, then each beat. given a beat whose harvest holds each value it proved and the state it left; beat 1: its row renders → the proof cell frames the thing being proven and nothing around it — no media toolbar, no dots, no `n / N` counter — with the whole screenshot one click away in the proof lightbox; the beat's position is read and walked on ONE stepper strip spanning both pictures, one segment per moment the beat proved, each named by the assertion the run recorded; beat 2: the reader opens → it opens in **step** — each beat held on its first scene — with the reader-wide controls (the **auto ↔ step** pair and the speed) on the requirement's title row, left of its ⋯ menu; beat 3: you walk a beat — its strip's `‹ ›`, a click on one of its named segments, or the ← → keys while its row is the **selected** one (visibly marked) — with ↑ ↓ selecting which When/Then and PgUp / PgDn paging the requirement → both pictures of that row move together to that one moment, the strip painting the segment they are on, the next chevron becoming a restart `↺` at the last moment that wraps to the first — and no other beat row moves; beat 4: you switch the play control to auto → every cell plays itself on a loop at the reader's speed; the speed control is live **only in auto** — a stepped beat sets its pace by hand; beat 5: the row is the Given → its one frame stays a plain, uncaptioned still — a state, not an action
